inspection_summary: Inspected all 510 normalized lines against the frozen source. The mathematical text runs from Euler's prime product and Dirichlet series through contour continuation, the functional symmetry, theta and centered xi representations, zero counting and the explicitly qualified real-zero conjecture, inverse Mellin/Fourier recovery of a weighted prime-power count, factorwise contour inversion with branch control, the explicit zero formula, squarefree inversion, and historical numerical diagnostics. Fifteen materially distinct units are retained, including both exact v1 spans. Page furniture and blanks are separated, and visibly damaged display extraction is flagged without silently repairing glyphs, limits, exponents, or differentials from outside the source.

sections_inspected.label: Opening and prime-encoding point of departure
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Frames prime accumulation and identifies the Euler product and integer Dirichlet series as two convergent representations of zeta.

sections_inspected.label: Mellin continuation and functional symmetry
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Passes from a positive-real Mellin integral to a keyhole contour, continues zeta, identifies the pole and negative-even zeros, and obtains the s to 1-s symmetry by reversing the contour and summing singular contributions.

sections_inspected.label: Theta reformulation and centered xi transform
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces a theta series, applies Jacobi's reciprocal-variable identity, symmetrizes the integral, and centers the completed function as xi(t) with cosine-integral representations.

sections_inspected.label: Zeros, conjectural location, and product representation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bounds the zero region, estimates zero count, distinguishes observed real zeros from the unproved all-real conjecture, records abandoned proof attempts, and represents log xi through its roots using a growth argument.

sections_inspected.label: Prime-power counting and transform inversion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines midpoint prime counting and its weighted prime-power smoothing, derives the log-zeta Mellin relation, inverts it via Fourier theory, and repairs a nonconvergent termwise substitution by integration by parts.

sections_inspected.label: Common factor kernels and branch-sensitive contour evaluation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reduces gamma and zero factors to a common inverse-transform form, evaluates the kernel in cases determined by the real part of a factor parameter, and fixes branches and constants through limiting paths.

sections_inspected.label: Explicit formula and ordering condition
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Combines pole, zeros, remaining integral, and constant into an explicit formula for the smoothed count while warning that the zero terms require magnitude ordering and are reorder-sensitive.

sections_inspected.label: Recovery, truncated density, and empirical diagnostics
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recovers the prime-counting function by squarefree alternating inversion, interprets finitely many zero terms as oscillatory density corrections, separates nonperiodic prime-power effects, and proposes empirical tracking of individual periodic terms.

accepted_units.title: Euler product as a bridge from primes to the integer Dirichlet series
accepted_units.why_material: The source begins from equality of a product indexed by primes and a series indexed by all positive integers, making multiplicative prime structure accessible through a function of a complex variable and recording the common half-plane of convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 3-9 supply historical motivation but are not required to state the mechanism. The product display at lines 12-16 has displaced glyphs; the prose at lines 17-21 supports only the representation-level claim used here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: verify the prime-product display in the page image before using exact typography or indices; no missing symbols have been reconstructed.

accepted_units.title: Mellin integral converted to a keyhole-contour continuation
accepted_units.why_material: A Mellin integral for the Dirichlet series is re-expressed through a contour around the origin with an explicit branch convention, producing a continuation that the source says is one-valued and finite except at 1 and vanishes at negative even integers.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose specifies the contour domain and logarithm branch. Page furniture interrupts the span at lines 56-59, and several integral limits and fraction bars are displaced, so the accepted content is the checked construction and stated consequences rather than a normalized formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula-layout dependence: scan verification is required for exact contour orientation, prefactors, limits, and gamma notation.

accepted_units.title: Contour reversal and residues expose the s to 1-s symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: For negative real part the source reverses the contour to enclose the other singularities, sums the contributions at integer multiples of 2 pi i, and concludes that a completed zeta expression is invariant under replacing s by 1-s.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit depends on the contour and branch setup in lines 35-60. The sum symbol at lines 75-76 and the completed-expression layout at lines 81-85 are extraction-damaged; the invariant statement at lines 79-86 is explicit prose evidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: use the prose-level deformation and symmetry claim unless the damaged displays are checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Gamma insertion turns the completed zeta into a theta Mellin transform
accepted_units.why_material: Motivated by the functional symmetry, the source inserts a half-argument gamma integral termwise, defines a theta-like sum psi, and rewrites the completed zeta as its Mellin integral. This is the bridge that makes reciprocal-variable symmetry available.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 87-93 give the purpose, lines 104-118 define psi and state the resulting integral. The display at lines 96-103 is badly aligned, so no exact exponent or normalization is inferred beyond what remains visible.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Image verification is required for the exact gamma integral, powers of pi and x, and summation indices.

accepted_units.title: Jacobi reciprocity symmetrizes the theta integral at x equals 1
accepted_units.why_material: The reciprocal-variable relation for psi is used to split and transform the Mellin integral, yielding a form with an elementary pole term and an integral whose paired powers display the functional symmetry.
accepted_units.context_note: The Jacobi relation is stated at lines 119-124 and the transformed equation occupies lines 130-149. The line-broken display is usable only for the structural split and pairing, not for exact transcription.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High display dependence: limits, half-powers, and coefficients need page-image verification before formula-level use.

accepted_units.title: Centering the completed function yields even cosine-integral representations
accepted_units.why_material: The substitution s equals one half plus t i defines xi(t), and the source gives cosine-integral forms that make dependence on t through an even kernel visible and support the subsequent statements that xi is finite and expandable in powers of t squared.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the missing antecedent for the carried v1 unit beginning 'This function' at line 171. Fractions are flattened in extraction, but the centering substitution, definition, and cosine dependence are visible.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: scan verification is needed for coefficients, derivatives, and powers in both integral representations.

accepted_units.title: Zero count, real-zero conjecture, failed proof search, and product from roots
accepted_units.why_material: The source confines possible zeros to a strip, gives an asymptotic count, reports finding approximately that many real roots, calls it very probable that all roots are real while explicitly wishing for a stricter proof and recording futile attempts, then uses zero density and growth to justify a logarithmic product representation up to a constant.
accepted_units.context_note: Exact v1 ID, type, and span are preserved. Lines 151-170 are required as antecedent context for xi(t); no claim stronger than the source's distinction among count, observation, probability, and proof gap is made.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependence: the counting display, half-widths, and product typography are damaged, but the conjectural status, abandoned attempt, root-density reasoning, and constant-at-t-equals-zero conclusion are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Weighted prime-power counting as the inverse transform of log zeta
accepted_units.why_material: The source defines a midpoint convention for the prime count, forms a weighted sum over prime powers, identifies log zeta divided by s as its Mellin transform, derives a vertical-line inverse using Fourier theory including the mean value at jumps, and identifies why direct integration of separated zero and gamma terms fails.
accepted_units.context_note: Exact v1 ID, type, and span are preserved. Lines 202-217 supply the root expansion substituted at lines 294-302, while lines 305-311 complete the integration-by-parts repair announced at lines 303-304.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: several exponents, roots, and integration variables are flattened; the definitions, transform direction, jump convention, and stated divergence are supported by adjacent prose.

accepted_units.title: Integration by parts repairs an invalid termwise explicit-formula route
accepted_units.why_material: After proposing substitution of the root-and-gamma expansion into the inverse transform, the source observes that the individual term integrals do not converge to infinity and changes the representation by integration by parts before evaluating factors separately.
accepted_units.context_note: This span deliberately overlaps the end of the carried Mellin bridge because it isolates a reusable obstruction-and-repair move. The exact differentiated display at lines 306-311 is not normalized beyond the source extraction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula verification is required for signs, the 1/log x prefactor, derivative placement, and contour notation; the nonconvergence diagnosis and integration-by-parts response are explicit prose.

accepted_units.title: Gamma and zero contributions are compressed to one inverse-transform kernel
accepted_units.why_material: A limiting product expansion for the gamma factor is differentiated, after which the source states that every nonconstant term in the expression for the smoothed count has a common factor-parameter integral form. This converts a heterogeneous decomposition into one reusable contour calculation.
accepted_units.context_note: The conceptual reduction is stated at lines 335-350, but the displays at lines 318-334 and 345-352 have displaced limits, sums, fractions, and parentheses. No exact generic kernel is silently repaired.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High extraction risk: retain only the source-stated common-form reduction pending scan verification of the gamma product and kernel.

accepted_units.title: Factor inversion splits by the sign of the parameter real part and fixes branches by limits
accepted_units.why_material: The source evaluates the generic factor contribution differently according as the factor parameter has negative or positive real part, obtains logarithmic-integral forms with different endpoints, and uses limiting imaginary or real directions to determine paths, branches, and integration constants.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose at lines 360, 372, and 400-419 supports the case distinction and branch logic. Most intervening displays are severely line-broken, including an ambiguous differential at lines 354-359, so the exact identities are not reconstructed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Scan-dependent: exact derivatives, signs, endpoints, branches, and constants must be verified from the page image before mathematical reuse.

accepted_units.title: The zero-based explicit formula requires magnitude ordering
accepted_units.why_material: The factor evaluations are combined into a formula for the smoothed prime-power count with a main logarithmic-integral term, paired zero contributions, an additional integral, and a constant; the source then specifies ordering zeros by magnitude and warns that reordering the series can produce an arbitrary real value.
accepted_units.context_note: The convergence and reorder-sensitivity statements at lines 433-455 are clear. The central formula at lines 422-432 and limiting integral at lines 439-452 are extraction-damaged, so this unit does not assert unverified coefficients or exponents.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula and ordering dependence: page-image verification is required before transcribing the explicit formula; magnitude ordering is part of the unit, not optional metadata.

accepted_units.title: Squarefree alternating inversion recovers the prime count from the smoothed count
accepted_units.why_material: The source inverts the weighted prime-power relation by summing over integers not divisible by any nontrivial square, with sign determined by the number of prime factors, thereby recovering F from values of f at fractional powers.
accepted_units.context_note: The inversion relation is stated in prose around the display, including the squarefree restriction and meaning of mu. Fractional exponents and coefficient placement are flattened in extraction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: verify exact summation and root typography from the scan; the squarefree alternating mechanism is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Finite zero sums model oscillatory prime-density corrections around nonperiodic terms
accepted_units.why_material: With finitely many zero terms, differentiating the smoothed explicit formula gives an approximate density whose cosine terms encode local oscillation; the source contrasts these with nonperiodic logarithmic-integral corrections from prime powers and states an order-scale limitation for the Li approximation.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose at lines 475-490 identifies truncation, density, periodic versus nonperiodic roles, and approximation scale. Displays at lines 480-482 and 491-493 are damaged, so coefficients, signs, and the precise error expression are not normalized here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence for quantitative use; retain only the qualitative decomposition and source-stated approximation limitation until scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Historical counts motivate tracking individual periodic terms and the smoother function f
accepted_units.why_material: The source compares Li with counts reported by Gauss and Goldschmidt, notes fluctuations and the absence of an observed law, proposes monitoring individual periodic terms in future counts, and suggests that the weighted function f behaves more regularly than F and agrees on average with the stated main expression in the observed range.
accepted_units.context_note: This is historical empirical evidence and a proposed diagnostic, not a proof or modern certification. Concrete ranges and qualitative observations are reported only as the source states them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low-to-moderate: prose carries the diagnostic; the final comparison includes a formula name whose constant should be retained exactly from the checked source if quoted.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From continuation to an even zero-bearing transform
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Within this source, contour continuation first extends zeta and exposes an s to 1-s relation; the theta Mellin representation and Jacobi reciprocity then recast that relation in a centered cosine-transform function suited to zero analysis.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a source-internal chain of representations, not a reconstructed proof at formula level; damaged prefactors, powers, and bounds require scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Zeros become prime-count information through convergence-aware inversion
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The root product is connected to a weighted prime-power count by inverse transform; a failed direct termwise route is repaired, each factor is evaluated with case and branch control, the zero series is ordered, and a squarefree alternating inversion recovers the prime count.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The synthesis records the source's mechanism and caveats only. It does not validate damaged formula details, remove the ordering condition, or turn the real-zero conjecture into a premise or proof.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite zero data supplies an oscillatory empirical diagnostic
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source interprets a finite selection of ordered zero terms as periodic corrections to prime-power density and proposes comparing individual oscillations with future counts when no local law had yet been observed.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Finite truncation is explicitly approximate, the reported counts are historical observations, and extraction damage prevents coefficient-level reuse without the scan.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Prime-power smoothing separates analytic structure from exact recovery
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The weighted prime-power function is both directly transformable through log zeta and reported as empirically more regular, while the original prime-counting function remains recoverable by squarefree alternating inversion.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The smoother-behavior claim is observational within the source, not a general theorem, and exact inversion typography remains formula-sensitive.
